statement: After an original-coordinate completion Q=a(X0+h)^2+R, if R has one original hub Y with nonzero slope m into a disjoint original bank J and projected crossing C=A_R[I,J](I-P_span(m)) with ||C||_F>0, then H_{1/2}(R)<=8(||m||||C||_F)^(-1/4), hence ||p_Q||_infinity<=8|a|^(-1/2)(||m||||C||_F)^(-1/4), with no row-marginal or rank condition on C.
mechanism: If the Z1 row law is spread, use reviewed k=1,ell=1 grouped projected crossing to obtain |phi_R(t)|<=min(1,2*pi*(||m||||C||_F)^(-1/2)|t|^-1), then the required half-Riesz Fourier potential. If a Z1 row is heavy, promote that literal original coordinate to a second hub; exact rank-two crossing gives a stronger |t|^-1 envelope. Finish with the required original-coordinate square peel.

required_source_used.application: Lemma 4.1 H_{1/2} Fourier potential and Lemma 4.2 square peel applied to the borderline |t|^-1 residual envelope.

partner_result_applied.application: On the new strict-N3 family C has rank one, so Z2=e_2(CC^T)=0 and the partner positive-Z2 theorem is unavailable; the new Z1 half-Riesz theorem gives a uniform 2^(11/4) bound.

strict_n3_family: A_xx=epsilon, A_yy=epsilon*nu, A_yJ=epsilon^-1 e^T, A_uJ=epsilon^-1 q^T with flat orthonormal e,q. It has at least four |eigenvalue|>1 for epsilon<=1/2, enters strict N3 as m grows, and has arbitrarily small nonzero pair singular value as nu->0. The new heavy-row branch gives ||p_Q||_infinity<=2^(11/4).
next_step: Route aligned states with C=0 or quantitatively tiny ||m||||C||_F to exact-singular random-slope, rank-one bilinear-plus-square, multi-hub, grouped-square, or another completed receiver before paying any reciprocal tiny pair singular value.
